    Macroeconomics and events

    The US data and Fed decisions markets watch; the gap between expectations and outcomes, and crypto-specific events.

    • How to read an economic calendar

      • Macroeconomics

      An economic calendar shows the time and importance of upcoming data releases and decisions, with their previous, expected and actual values, in a single table.

    • Priced in: why expectations matter

      • Macroeconomics

      Markets react to events not only when they happen but from the moment they are expected.

    • Fed rate decisions (FOMC)

      • Macroeconomics

      The Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) sets the US Federal Reserve's policy rate at eight scheduled meetings a year.

    • Inflation data (CPI, PCE)

      • Macroeconomics

      In the US, inflation is followed every month through two main releases: the Consumer Price Index (CPI) from the BLS and the Personal Consumption Expenditures (PCE) price index from the BEA.

    • Jobs data (nonfarm payrolls, jobless claims)

      • Macroeconomics

      US jobs data shows how strong the labour market is.

    • Growth data (GDP, PMI)

      • Macroeconomics

      Growth data shows how fast the US economy is expanding or slowing.

    • Bond yields and the yield curve

      • Macroeconomics

      The yield on US Treasuries sums up the market's rate, growth and inflation expectations in a single number.

    • The dollar index (DXY)

      • Macroeconomics

      The dollar index (DXY) measures the US dollar against six major currencies in a single number.

    • Stock indices and risk appetite

      • Macroeconomics

      The S&P 500 and Nasdaq 100 are indices that sum up the overall direction of the US stock market, and they are widely used to read the market's risk appetite.

    • Crypto-specific events: token unlocks, halvings, ETF flows

      • Macroeconomics

      Token unlocks, the Bitcoin halving, spot ETF flows and network upgrades are events specific to the crypto market.
